clause.quote: A set of controller-indexed signatures on a non-key event message (see below) MUST at least satisfy the signing threshold for the establishment event indicated by the event reference in the attachment group (which MAY or MAY NOT be the current signing threshold) to be accepted as valid.

inferred_from.inference: The sentence states a condition for a non-key-event message to be accepted as valid, not that a validator must accept one that meets it. No sentence obliges a validator to accept an exchange message, so that it should accept one that passes every check is inferred and graded SHOULD, as liveness is in the rest of the KERI layer (docs/design.md, IPEX).

description: The sender opens a transaction with an exchange inception (xip) and continues it with an exn whose x and p are both the xip's SAID, each signed by the sender's current key. A validator should accept both (liveness, inferred). The first message of a transaction MUST be an xip (KERI line 979), so an implementation that starts transactions without one, or does not process xip, fails this case.

clauses.quote: The first message MUST be an Exchange Inception message with type `xip`.

dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-09; not yet raised with keripy or the KERI specification working group.
dispute.summary: KERI line 979 says the first message of a transaction MUST be an exchange inception (xip), and x MUST be its SAID, so a validator should accept a well-formed, signed xip and the exn that continues it. keripy main (9a8b7aa7) does not process an exchange inception: Kevery.processXip is a stub ('no processing yet', src/keri/core/eventing.py), so it accepts no xip and reports every one rejected. The exn is accepted. keripy's own IPEX opens an exchange with an exn whose x is the digest of a fresh nonce rather than the SAID of an xip (apply, offer and grant in src/keri/acdc/ipexing.py), a reading of transactions the text does not support.

title: A well-formed exchange transaction
